newsitem.title: UK: IBCA gives Malayan Banking Berhad rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA gives Malayan Banking Berhad rating.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 3 - IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has assigned an Individual rating of B to Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) and affirmed the bank's Legal rating of 2.
It is Malaysia's largest bank and has a strong overall financial profile with a track record of good management and strong financial performance.

Maybank would be the most profitable of the Malaysian banks if not for its very conservative general provisioning policy, which has resulted in a level of general loan loss reserves more than twice that of the other banks. It has some of the lowest expense ratios among local banks.

Asset quality has improved markedly over the past few years and non-performing loans are now just 3.4% of gross loans compared to 9.4% in 1991. Furthermore, non-performing loans are classified according to a stricter definition than required by the central bank.
The parent bank's risk weighted capital adequacy ratio will rise to 16.4%, the highest ratio among local banks, with the just announced sale of Kwong Yik Bank.

A bank's Individual rating is an evaluation of its financial strength based on the premise that the bank is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners. A rating of B is the third highest Individual rating level awarded by IBCA, while the highest awarded is A.
Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if the rated bank were to run into difficulties.

A Legal Rating of 2 indicates that, in the agency's opinion, support would be provided to Maybank should it encounter difficulties even though there is no explicit guarantee of support from the Government. IBCA notes that Bank Negara, the Malaysian central bank, has a long history of fully supporting banks in difficulties.
